Subject: Persistent chat disconnects during peak window (logs attached)

Laura —

We're seeing a recurrence of the chat sessions "ghosting" behavior in our production integration. Between 08:00-11:30 PST this morning ~12% of user sessions lost the stream mid-response; clients reported immediate 502/504 or timeout errors, and a smaller but noticeable fraction received repeated 429s when the client retried. We've attached a small sample of session logs and a timeline in the spreadsheet.

This is impacting our triage nurses who depend on interactive transcripts — we had to force-failover to our legacy pipeline which increased latency and caused a backlog. Can you confirm whether there was a capacity event or a routing fallback that could explain the elevated 5xx/429s? We need a short written summary for our incident review and an ETA on mitigation.

Attached: session-sample-logs.txt (12KB), orion-incident-timeline.xlsx

Thanks,
Arjun
Senior Product Manager — Orion Health

Arjun — thank you for the fast heads-up and the logs. I'm escalating this to our incident response (cc'd) and looping in Sean for exec visibility.

Quick notes from my side:
- We see correlated error spikes in our anomaly dashboard starting 08:12 PST — elevated 5xx and a cluster of 429s concentrated on the US-west serving pool.
- Initial hypothesis: a routing pressure event caused several requests to be proxied to a fallback model variant which produced slower-than-expected token throughput; client SDK retry logic caused request bursts (retry storm) leading to additional 429s.

I'm requesting Marcus and Monica to take ownership of triage: 1) determine whether this was a serving capacity shortage or kernel-level timeouts, 2) identify short-term mitigations (fallback throttles / immediate routing fix), 3) produce a timeline and remediation ETA.

Arjun, we'll reply with a customer-facing summary within 2 hours and a next-step plan. Thanks for sending the artifacts.

Best,

Subject: Re: Persistent chat disconnects during peak window (logs attached) — Triage notes

Looping notes from infra triage (quick, not exhaustive):
- Confirmed token generation latencies for the affected model variant increased by ~3x between 08:10-08:45 PST. In several cases the K/V cache priming was delayed due to a high eviction churn on node gw-west-12.
- There was a transient autoscaler decision that delayed bursting additional pods behind the pool for ~90s — autoscaler thresholds didn't trigger until retry traffic amplified.
- Observed client SDK patterns show aggressive immediate retries (0s, 200ms, 500ms) which generated concentrated load on the fallback path.

SHORT-TERM MITIGATIONS (applied):
- Temporarily lowered the retry budget for fallback routes to suppress client-side retry amplification. (Applied at 10:12)
- Forced re-route of the impacted customer traffic to an alternate west pool with warm caches (10:18).
- Increased ephemeral capacity on west pool by +30% (10:22) to absorb burst.

Next actions:
- Monica to prepare customer-facing timeline and confirm if any user data was affected.
- I will open a kernel-level investigation ticket and add traces to REDINF-8921 for follow-up.

We should prepare a short exec note for leadership summarizing impact hours, mitigation steps, and SLAs at risk.

Marcus
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Persistent chat disconnects during peak window (final customer summary & next steps)

Arjun / Orion team —

Appreciate your patience while we completed investigation and mitigations. Below is a concise summary you can use for your incident review. Please let me know if you'd like us to join a postmortem call.

1) Impact summary- Window: 2026-11-28 08:10–08:50 PST- Affected sessions: ~12% of active interactive chats during window (sampled-based estimate)- Symptoms: mid-response stream termination, client-visible 502/504 on long responses; subsequent 429s from client retries

2) Root cause (short form)- A combination of: (a) temporary autoscaler lag on the US-west serving pool leading to under-provisioned serving capacity, (b) higher than normal KV-cache eviction churn on gw-west-12 which increased per-token compute time, and (c) aggressive client retry behavior amplified traffic when latencies rose, producing localized 429s (retry storm) and additional 5xx responses as nodes became overloaded.

3) Mitigation steps taken (immediate)- Lowered fallback retry budget to reduce amplification (temporary policy change applied 10:12 PST)- Force-routed Orion traffic to a warm pool with healthy caches (10:18 PST)- Added ephemeral capacity to west pool (+30% soak) while autoscaler thresholds were tuned (10:22 PST)

4) Short-term fixes (next 7 days)- Auto-scaler threshold tuning to reduce lag in burst start-up- Adjust serving pool cache eviction policy and investigate long-tail eviction causes on gw-west-12- SDK guidance for customers: adopt jittered exponential backoff default in the next minor SDK release and a recommended retry budget (we will provide patch notes)

5) Longer-term actions- Instrumentation improvements to detect early K/V eviction cascades- Circuit-breaker patterns for fallback model variants to avoid proxying disproportionate traffic to slower backends- Customer SDK and server-side cooperative throttling playbook

Customer ask / SLA note: We recognize this affected availability for a subset of your users during the window. We're not seeing evidence of data loss; transcripts were not dropped at rest. We will prepare an official post-incident report (standard template) and propose a 30-minute postmortem sync next week.

If Apollo (exec sponsor) or anyone from the Orion ops leadership wants a short briefing, Laura / Sean are available.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
